name: Tiaoxin-346
workload: Long message (>=2048 bytes) with long associated data, AES-NI-optimized C implementation (crypto_aead/tiaoxinv2/nim), measured as cycles/byte on a real CPU via the eBACS/SUPERCOP timing harness.
claimed_speedup: ~4.7x lower cycles/byte than aes256gcmv1 (0.15 vs 0.70 median cycles/byte, long+long encrypt) (derived from page data)
hardware: amd64, Raptor Cove P-cores, 2024 Intel Core 5 210H, 4 x 2200MHz (eBACS machine "freshwrap,big")
stars_or_usage: 104 stars (floodyberry/supercop mirror); algorithm still included in current eBACS/SUPERCOP releases (page shows dataset supercop-20260627)
tradeoffs: Not NIST/IETF standardized, no TLS/library adoption; requires AES-NI; smaller 128-bit security margin scrutiny than AES-GCM; CAESAR-competition cipher (finalist, high-performance use case) rather than a production-hardened library.
caveats: Comparison is against SUPERCOP's own generic aes256gcmv1 reference/optimized implementation (not literally the OpenSSL codebase, though the same AES-GCM construction). GitHub mirror (floodyberry/supercop) is a stale 2016 snapshot; numbers come from the live, continuously-updated bench.cr.yp.to results page (supercop-20260627 dataset) rather than a commit in this specific mirror. Table column is median (50%) of 25/50/75th percentile cycles/byte; compiler used by the SUPERCOP harness is not stated on this results page, capping tier at B.
found_via: GitHub: gh search code "Tiaoxin-346" -> floodyberry/supercop:crypto_aead/tiaoxinv2; cross-checked against eBACS AEAD results page for the algorithm name

name: AEZ (v4)
workload: Long message (>=2048 bytes) with long associated data, AES-NI implementation (crypto_aead/aezv4/aesni), measured as cycles/byte on a real CPU via the eBACS/SUPERCOP timing harness.
claimed_speedup: ~2.7x lower cycles/byte than aes256gcmv1 (0.26 vs 0.70 median cycles/byte, long+long encrypt) (derived from page data)
hardware: amd64, Raptor Cove P-cores, 2024 Intel Core 5 210H, 4 x 2200MHz (eBACS machine "freshwrap,big")
stars_or_usage: 104 stars (floodyberry/supercop mirror); still included in current eBACS/SUPERCOP releases
tradeoffs: Non-standard, misuse-resistant (nonce-reuse-resistant) AEAD with variable-length tags/nonces, wide-block-cipher design (AEZ) rather than a stream+MAC AEAD; not adopted in any mainstream TLS/library stack; the design underwent several security revisions (v1-v5) after cryptanalytic findings, and this repo only mirrors v3/v4 (not the latest v5).
caveats: Public-domain dedication (Ted Krovetz, 'free and unencumbered software'), so 'no patent grant' applies. Baseline is SUPERCOP's own aes256gcmv1, not literally OpenSSL. Mirror is a stale 2016 snapshot; numbers are read from the live bench.cr.yp.to page (supercop-20260627 dataset). Compiler not stated on this results page, capping tier at B.
found_via: GitHub: gh search code "AEZ" "authenticated encryption" -> floodyberry/supercop:crypto_aead/aezv4; cross-checked against eBACS AEAD results page

name: MORUS-1280
workload: Long message (>=2048 bytes) with long associated data, AVX2 implementation (crypto_aead/morus1280256v1/avx2), measured as cycles/byte on a real CPU via the eBACS/SUPERCOP timing harness.
claimed_speedup: ~1.06x lower cycles/byte than aes256gcmv1 (0.66 vs 0.70 median cycles/byte, long+long encrypt) (derived from page data)
hardware: amd64, Raptor Cove P-cores, 2024 Intel Core 5 210H, 4 x 2200MHz (eBACS machine "freshwrap,big")
stars_or_usage: 104 stars (floodyberry/supercop mirror); still included in current eBACS/SUPERCOP releases
tradeoffs: Margin over AES-GCM is small (~6%) on this AES-NI-equipped CPU and within measurement noise on some other machines/sections of the same page; not standardized, not adopted in production stacks; ARX/AES-round hybrid CAESAR finalist.
caveats: Speedup on this specific machine is marginal (~6%), much smaller than Tiaoxin-346/AEZ's margins; on other message-size sections of the same page the gap narrows further. No license header found in the source files in this repo (CAESAR-era submission, terms unclear) - treat as reference/study-only, not redistribute-and-relicense. Baseline is SUPERCOP's own aes256gcmv1, not literally OpenSSL. Mirror is a stale 2016 snapshot.
